issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to use a List implemented with an ArrayList for the animals attribute, but the solution implements the animals attribute as a Queue<Animal> backed by a LinkedList. This mismatch between the specified collection type (List/ArrayList) and the solution's Queue/LinkedList can confuse students about the intended API (getter/setter types and expected collection semantics) and about how to implement addAnimal/feedAllAnimals and singFarmSong iteration.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by using a List<Animal> backed by an ArrayList (e.g., private List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>();) and update the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if Queue semantics were intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify Queue/LinkedList everywhere so students know which collection type and API to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires the Farm to hold its animals in a List and explicitly instructs initializing an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor. The solution, however, declares the animals field as a Queue<Animal> and initializes it with a LinkedList. This type/name discrepancy (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) refers to the same conceptual collection of animals but uses different type identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students about the expected collection type and how to implement the getter/setter/addAnimal methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the collection type across artifacts. Either change the solution to use List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>() (and keep getAnimals()/setAnimals() signatures using List), or update the problem statement and template instructions to accept Queue/LinkedList consistently. Prefer changing the solution to use List/ArrayList to match the explicit requirement in the problem statement.
